articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations' (Digest no.124)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,

articleTitle: Supplier's works (Part V of the regulations)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,
abstract: The regulations for suppliers works from the 1988 Electricity Supply Regulations are discussed. They include limiting electric lines to 440000 V, safety requirements of substations, requirements for inspection of works and taking account of time for which current passes after failure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Miscellaneous (part VII of the regulations) (1988 Electricity Supply Regulations)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,
abstract: The author presents areas of the 1988 Electricity Supply Regulations which are covered in any other sections. These include the reporting of accidents where no-one is hurt, the reporting of supply failure, the requirement to keep maps of networks and being allowed to serve notice on a supplier if their works is in breach of the regulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Introduction to the Electricity Supply Regulations 1988
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,
abstract: 1988 was the year when the Electricity Supply Regulations were combined and placed under one cover. The regulations have moved away from the previous practice of defining requirements in terms of detailed technical design. Overlaps with other regulations are reduced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Underground cables and overhead lines (parts III and IV of the regulations)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,
abstract: Most accidents involving underground cables are caused by authorities not locating the lines correctly. Two regulations are presented, the first requires that all cables be screened and the second that they are put below a certain depth. Regulations for overhead lines are also discussed with particular reference to the materials used for support.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Supply to consumers installations (part VI of the regulations)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,
abstract: The 1988 Electricity Supply Regulations for supplies to consumers installations are discussed. The supplier now has to give any information on his system to the consumer if required. Variations in the supply are now covered to be within certain limits. Suppliers are also now allowed to withhold supply to the consumer if he suspects danger or interference.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Revision of Electricity Supply Regulations,
abstract: In the 1988 Electricity Supply Regulations there is now a separate section for earthing. Various particular regulations are dealt with which discuss: making conductors appear dead if the neutral is disconnected; earthing of systems at different voltages; multiple earthing; and changing of installations to present regulations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
